result.title: On the Feature Evolution of Temporal Difference Learning
result.summary: Temporal-difference (TD) learning trains neural representations using bootstrapped targets generated by evolving value estimates, yet how predictive features emerge and propagate under incomplete neural updates remains poorly understood. We investigate this problem using finite-width two-layer ReLU critics on a constructed family of smooth stochastic horizon-$H$ MDPs with unknown quadratic structure and $d$-dimensional observations. We first show that an informative TD update acquires the quadratic Bellman signal and yields a representation admitting a bounded predictive readout. The simultaneous hidden-weight and head update achieves a strict finite-sample prediction-risk improvement over matched head-only SGD, with a $2(d+1)$-fold larger population quadratic response. We then establish that an imperfect learned continuation can already provide informative supervision to an earlier zero-reward stage. By tracking coupled neural updates with one SGD step per target copy, without requiring intermediate Bellman regressions to be solved, we obtain a uniform prediction-error transient $\exp[-Ω(K/(Hd))]$, up to action-independent shifts and explicit sampling and finite-width errors. On the constructed signed-action MDP family whose total reward is bounded by 1, we show that an exploration-then-commit algorithm can achieve $\widetilde{O}(d^3H^{1/3}T^{2/3})$ regret over $T$ episodes, using $K=\widetilde{O}(Hd)$ global updates. Our analysis connects bootstrapped feature acquisition, concurrent neural refinement, and finite-budget policy performance.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在构造的平滑随机 horizon-H MDP 上，用有限宽度两层 ReLU critic 分析 TD 学习中二次 Bellman 信号如何被习得、预测性特征如何在隐层与读出头联合更新中形成，并给出有限更新预算下的 regret 界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不完美的后续估计仍能为更早阶段提供有用监督」及用单步 SGD 追踪耦合更新的分析，可能为 LVR 多阶段 latent 轨迹的 bootstrap 式监督与贡献分配提供可核查的理论视角，但本身不涉及视觉推理。
